OET SAMPLE TEST: MEDICINE
CANDIDATE CARD


SETTING      Suburban General Practice


DOCTOR
The mother/father of 7-year-old Cody, has brought her/his son today
because s/he is worried about the boy’s behaviour. He has problems
sitting still and concentrating. He often breaks items and has been
getting into trouble at school from his behaviour. His mother/father
has come to you for some advice and help. You are a doctor with
high principles who will not prescribe drugs to children unless you
consider them to be absolutely necessary. You have been the boy’s
GP since his birth. His mother/father is single with no partner that
you are aware of.


TASK
   •   Ask the mother/father her reasons for bringing Cody for the
       consultation
   •   Mention the possibility that the boy does not suffer from ADHD
       but there may be other factors causing his behaviour, e.g. lack
       of regular routine, food allergies.
   •   Ask about his diet.
   •   If ADHD is diagnosed, suggest non-drug treatments, e.g.
       behaviour therapy, neuro-feedback
   •   Be insistent that you will not prescribe Ritalin or any other drug
       unless it is absolutely necessary and only after a complete
       examination of the boy
   •   Suggest a blood test and follow up appointment for further
       examination
